step1_analysis.circuit_type: DC Offset Cancellation (DCOC) / Active Feedback Loop
step1_analysis.description: This circuit forms an active negative feedback loop (Gm-C filter) for an Intermediate Frequency (IF) amplifier. It senses the DC voltage at the IF node, integrates the error on capacitor C, and feeds back a correction current via T10/T11 to stabilize the DC operating point and remove low-frequency offsets.

paper_reference.title: Remotely Powered Addressable UHF RFID Integrated System

dc_power.description: Total DC power consumption of the feedback loop.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the exact bias voltages applied to Iref_p and Iref_n, but typical baseband analog blocks in RFID consume very low power.

if_dc_voltage.description: Steady-state DC bias voltage established at the IF node by the feedback loop.

sky130_expected.calculation: The T1/T4 inverter threshold determines the settling point. With VDD=1.8V, it settles near VDD/2.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Negative feedback forces the IF node to the switching threshold of the T1/T4 input stage.

ac_impedance_100k.description: AC impedance magnitude at 100 kHz, showing the active inductor / high-pass effect.

sky130_expected.calculation: At low frequencies, the high loop gain reduces the impedance at the IF node.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The feedback loop is active at 100 kHz, shunting AC currents to maintain the DC point.

ac_impedance_10M.description: AC impedance magnitude at 10 MHz, where the feedback loop is disabled by the capacitor.

sky130_expected.calculation: At high frequencies, C1 shorts V_C to ground, breaking the loop. Impedance is determined by parasitic capacitance.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The circuit acts as a high-pass filter for the IF signal, so high-frequency impedance must be large to avoid attenuating the signal.

settling_time.description: Time required for the IF node to return to its DC bias point after a transient current step.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the typical timing metrics reported in the paper for baseband settling.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, power consumption, AC impedance profile (active inductor behavior), and transient settling time of the DCOC loop.
